settings.headline: Open 5:00 am to 11:00 pm, every day
settings.subtitle: Cadwallow Park is a fictional 410-acre city park with four gates, a lake called the Wallow, a wooded ridge and a long meadow. Entry is free. Here is how to get here, what the rules are and what to expect.

items.title: Route 14 to the South Gate
items.text: Every 12 minutes on weekdays, every 20 at weekends. The stop is at the gate.

items.title: City bike path to the West Gate
items.text: The path joins the Perimeter Path at the Meadow Street crossing. Racks at every gate.

items.title: Ridge Road or the East Gate
items.text: 40 spaces at the North Gate, 12 accessible spaces at the East Gate. Free, no time limit.

items.title: From downtown
items.text: Three miles along the river greenway, ending at the South Gate.

settings.headline: Park rules, in plain words
settings.intro: From the city park ordinance (fictional). Crew and park rangers will remind you; they would rather not have to.

items.why: Woods trails close at dusk because there is no lighting under the trees.
Off-leash only 6–9 am in the Long Meadow kite field. Bag it and bin it.

items.rule: Bikes on the paved paths only
items.why: Not on the Ridge Trail, the boardwalk or the Meadow Path.

items.rule: Off the ice unless posted open
items.why: The crew post the Wallow open at 5 inches of clear ice, and not before.
Foraging and collecting are not allowed in city parks.
No open fires anywhere else. Hot coals go in the red bins.

items.a: No. The park, the trails, the playground and the Walled Garden are free. Rowboats and shelter reservations have fees, paid at the boathouse or the park office.
Only with a permit from the Parks and Recreation office. Call (555) 014-2200.
Not in the Wallow. The Splash Pad runs June to August, and the city pool is two blocks east of the East Gate.
The Wallow Loop, the Perimeter Path and the Elm Walk are step-free. Each trail page says how accessible it is.
